title: Chapter 9 Revision: Verbal Nouns
description: Test your knowledge of verbal noun formation, aspect distinction, and usage in Polish.

questions.prompt: How do you form a verbal noun from an imperfective verb like 'czytać'?
questions.explanation: Imperfective verbs ending in -ać form verbal nouns with -anie: czytać → czytanie, gotować → gotowanie.

questions.prompt: Which verbal noun comes from a PERFECTIVE verb?
questions.explanation: Przeczytanie comes from przeczytać (perfective). It refers to the completed act of reading through. Czytanie, pisanie, mówienie are from imperfective verbs.

questions.prompt: Lubię ___ (read/the act of reading). [use imperfective verbal noun]
questions.explanation: After lubić, use the imperfective verbal noun (genitive after negation, accusative after positive). Czytanie (imperfective) = the ongoing enjoyment of reading as an activity.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Po ___ książki (after finishing/reading through the book), poszłam spać.'
questions.explanation: After 'po' we need the locative case and a perfective verbal noun (completed action). Przeczytaniu is the locative of przeczytanie (perfective).

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses 'po + verbal noun'?
questions.explanation: Po + locative of PERFECTIVE verbal noun. Napisaniu is correct (locative of napisanie, from napisać perfective). Po pisaniu would imply 'after a period of writing' without completion.
Palenie (verbal noun from palić) acts as a subject here. In signs and formal notices, verbal nouns are commonly used as subjects.

questions.prompt: What is the verbal noun from 'wychodzić' (to be leaving/exiting)?
questions.explanation: Wychodzić (imperfective) → wychodzenie. Note: wyjście is from wyjść (perfective), which is also a common verbal noun meaning 'exit/the act of leaving (completed)'.
Uczenie się polskiego wymaga cierpliwości. The reflexive verbal noun 'uczenie się' (learning) is the subject; polskiego is genitive (of Polish); cierpliwości is genitive after wymagać.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct ending for this formal sign: 'WEJŚCIE ___'
questions.explanation: Wejście is neuter, so the adjective agrees: wzbronione (neuter nominative). WEJŚCIE WZBRONIONE = No entry / Entry forbidden.

questions.prompt: Which sentence shows a verbal noun as a direct object?
questions.explanation: In 'Lubię gotowanie', gotowanie is the direct object (accusative) of lubić. In the other sentences it serves as subject, locative complement, or genitive object.

questions.prompt: Nie lubię ___ (doing homework). [verbal noun from 'odrabiać' + 'lekcji'/'prac domowych']
questions.explanation: After 'nie lubić' use the genitive. The verbal noun odrabiania (genitive of odrabianie, from odrabiać) + lekcji (genitive). 'Nie lubię odrabiania lekcji.'

questions.prompt: What is the key difference between 'czytanie' and 'przeczytanie'?
options: Czytanie = ongoing process; przeczytanie = completed action
Czytanie = past tense; przeczytanie = present tense
There is no difference; they are synonyms
questions.explanation: Czytanie (from imperfective czytać) refers to reading as an ongoing activity or process. Przeczytanie (from perfective przeczytać) refers to a completed reading. This aspect distinction is preserved in verbal nouns.
